content:
Bloomberg reported that Apple may release a new Mac mini "as early as the next few days," potentially ahead of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra launch event expected next month. Here are the details.

It is likely the last product launch event of Tim Cook's tenure

According to Mark Gurman, Apple is "preparing to release the first update to its Mac mini desktop in nearly two years," with some of the recent demand increase coming from users hoping to run AI applications and models locally.

Report details:

Gurman added that Apple "has tested versions with both M5 and M6 generation processors," differing from the new iMac expected to feature the M6 chip.

Just weeks before tonight's report, Apple once again reiterated that it would begin producing Mac mini at its Houston facility later this year, when Tim Cook was visiting the plant alongside Trump administration officials.

The same site houses Apple's brand-new Advanced Manufacturing Center, which has already begun producing and shipping the company's AI servers. Apple stated earlier this month that it has invested hundreds of millions of dollars into the facility in less than nine months.

It remains unclear whether the new Mac mini launching in the next few days is the same model Apple plans to produce in Houston later this year, but based on various indications, the chances appear quite high.

Gurman also reiterated in his report multiple details about Apple's Mac product line plans for the coming months:

More Mac products will be陆续推出, but the timing is expected to be further out. These include an iMac with new color options, and an updated entry-level MacBook Pro. Both will use the M6 chip, the next-generation processor. The most anticipated Mac in the lineup will be Apple's first computer with a touchscreen. Apple will add this feature to a brand-new MacBook Pro model, offering 14-inch and 16-inch options, with a redesigned chassis and OLED display.

Looking further ahead, Gurman reiterated earlier reports that Apple plans to launch new MacBook Air and MacBook Neo models next year, as well as a second-generation touchscreen MacBook Pro with the M7 chip.
